Chris Henry

Progressive, Pacific Green candidate for US Senator, Oregon · Challenger

Long-haul union truck driver

Chris Henry is a long-haul union truck driver and former aircraft mechanic who has served as co-chair of the Oregon Progressive Party. He is the nominee of both the Progressive and Pacific Green parties for U.S. Senate in Oregon's November 3, 2026 general election, according to the state voters' pamphlet. He has run for office several times since 2008, including as the Progressive nominee for U.S. Senate in 2022.

Where Henry stands

Labor
Supports full unionization of all workers, making Oregon a union card-check state, and stronger overtime rules, including time and a half after 8 hours a day and 40 hours a week.
High prices / cost of living
Proposes a $15/hour standard minimum wage and a $20/hour prevailing minimum wage, each rising $0.25 a year for 20 years, plus a maximum wage capped at a 10:1 pay ratio.
Health care
Supports universal Medicare for All covering mental health, dental, vision, and alternative care such as naturopathy, chiropractic, and acupuncture.
Democracy and elections
Supports ranked-choice voting, multi-member districts, a single-chamber (unicameral) legislature, campaign finance reform, and disclosure rules for campaign ads.
Climate change
Proposes ending fossil fuel and logging subsidies and moving them to industrial hemp. Also supports a tree-planting 'ArborCorps' and a new Civilian Conservation Corps-style federal jobs program.
Taxes
Supports raising taxes on the wealthy and prosecuting people who avoid taxes by moving money offshore.
Banking
Proposes an Oregon state bank and publicly owned city, county, and regional banks, and calls for divesting from Wall Street.
Military and foreign policy
Advocates closing all overseas U.S. military bases, bringing troops home, and creating an Oregon Department of Peace funded by moving war-related tax dollars elsewhere.
Education
Supports publicly funded education from daycare and pre-K through trade training, higher education, and lifelong learning.

Background

  • Occupation: long-haul union truck driver (Teamsters Local 81, per Smarter.vote); third-generation trucker
  • Former aircraft mechanic at Rockwell and McDonnell Douglas
  • Former union shop steward and organizer
  • Co-chair of the Oregon Progressive Party
  • Education: Clackamas Community College; Portland State University; UAW Trade School (per voters' pamphlet, as reported)
  • Progressive nominee for U.S. Senate in Oregon, 2022 (36,883 votes, 1.91%)
  • Past campaigns, per Smarter.vote: Oregon Labor Commissioner, Oregon Treasurer, Multnomah County Commission, Portland City Council
